basis: Glycogen synthesis disorder defined by skeletal muscle and cardiac glycogen deficiency, with myopathy and cardiomyopathy; seizures are occasional (5-29%).
Inflammation of the lacrimal gland; the umbrella diagnosis does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Acromesomelic skeletal dysplasia; complete atrioventricular block was reported in 1/2 patients (~50%), supporting cardiovascular involvement despite the small sample.
Esophageal leiomyomas define gastrointestinal disease; vulvar tumors have no axis. Alport ancestry alone does not establish common nephropathy for this specific concept.
Congenital cleft involves the laryngeal/tracheal and esophageal partition, causing severe swallowing dysfunction and pulmonary damage.
Skin lesions and cardiac defects define syndrome; intellectual disability/seizures and sensorineural hearing loss each reported in 1/1 assessed. Skeletal features omitted at four-axis cap.
Disease localized to the spinal cord; additional organ damage is not shared across this broad group.
Progressive brainstem and white-matter degeneration defines disease; vomiting, eye-movement abnormalities and auditory evoked changes do not establish separate organ damage.
Developmental defects of skin, sweat glands, hair and nails, together with characteristic dental hypoplasia and malformations.
Malignant mesothelial tumor arising in the pericardium.
Microvascular thrombosis with hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia defines TMA; direct renal microangiopathic injury is common (>30%). Neurologic injury varies by subtype.
Inflammation localized to the trachea and bronchi; this broad diagnosis does not specify an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Granulomatous lesion of the ocular orbit; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Reflex epilepsy triggered by sound; acoustic triggering does not imply ear damage.
Developmental disability and epilepsy define syndrome. Frequent small nails do not establish functional skin damage; ocular and limb defects are mostly occasional (5-29%).
Cancer arising in the lacrimal apparatus, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Congenital absence of optic nerve and retinal structures is ocular. CNS malformations accompany bilateral cases, but involvement in at least 30% overall is not established.
Cerebrospinal fluid-filled spinal nerve-root cysts; radiculopathy reflects nerve-root disease.
Marrow lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with IgM paraprotein; not an inborn metabolic disorder. Pulmonary lesions are <30%; respiratory insufficiency alone does not prove direct lung damage.
Benign tumor arising in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes; smooth muscle histology does not make it skeletal muscle disease.
Corneal dystrophy, keratoderma/nail abnormalities and skeletal defects define syndrome; dental enamel abnormalities affect 80-99%, supporting oral GI involvement. Hearing loss is <30%.
Congenital acral skin hyperpigmentation defines the disease.
A form of keratitis, localized to the cornea; no specific infectious or immune-mediated etiology is established.
Genetic susceptibility subtype of schizophrenia, a purely psychiatric disorder without established damage to an included organ axis.
Inherited metabolic neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation and cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus and dysphagia do not establish intrinsic ocular or gastrointestinal damage.
